description: The comparison of CAA records in the monitoring of a gateway, RELAY-v0.md section 6.7: one evaluation of the answers for one name. Each case: the name that was queried (the standard name, or the apex of the name domain), the pair (CAA identity and ACME account) in force that the gateway knows, or null while no account is in force; the minutes since the pairing; the state of the one-hour excuse for the record that was prescribed before a new pair (null, or the earlier pair or null, whether the gateway reported it itself, and the minutes since it learned the new pair); whether the answers are DNSSEC-validated; and the answers of the resolvers. Each resolver has a provider (resolvers of one provider count as one), a status (ok, or nxdomain, which is an empty answer, or a failure: servfail, refused, formerr, timeout, truncated, unparsable), the CNAME or DNAME records that the answer followed, and the CAA records (flags, tag, value). Result: difference (the gateway counts a difference: some resolver that answered shows a record that is not prescribed or excused, also when the round is not a successful query) or prescribed (it counts none: every answer is as prescribed or excused, no resolver answered, or the standard name is not checked yet). A failed query is no difference, and a resolver that fails is left out. Where a case has successful_round, it says whether the round counts as a successful query for the 24 hours of Section 6.7 (at least two independent resolvers answered, resolvers of one provider counting as one, or the answers are DNSSEC-validated); it never changes the result. A difference raises an alarm only after the repeat of Section 6.7, which the cases do not cover.
